newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian c.bank chief says litas to stay stable.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian c.bank chief says litas to stay stable.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank chief Reinoldijus Sarkinas said late on Monday that the country's currency, the litas, would remain stable for the forseeable future.
"The litas is stable and will remain stable," Sarkinas told Reuters after meeting with the heads of commercial banks and the country's prime minister-designate Gediminas Vagnorius.
The victory by Vagnorius' Homeland Union party in last week's parliamentary elections sparked a run on the dollar in local banks.
The local market was responding to Vagnorius' post-election pledge to scrap the country's currency board, a move which many believe would lead to devaluation.
The currency board regime, introduced in April 1994, bars the central bank from using exchabge or interest rates as monetary tools.
Instead, the bank gurantees that it will maintain one U.S. dollar in its reserves for every four litas in circulation, freezing the exchange rate at that level.
"All sides agree that there is no basis for panic. The situation is stable and the run for dollars has slowed," Sarkinas said.
He added that the currency board would be abolished gradually.
"The currency board was very necessary when the the litas was introduced because it eliminated political intrusion in the exchange rate...(But) in the long run, it ties up the central bank," he said.
